correctness.rationale: The graph has 20 vertices and 30 verified edges; the closed-neighborhood characterization of the dominance complex is exact. Two independent membership tests agree for every one of 1,048,576 masks. A full acyclic staged matching has 217,103 pairs and only a critical vertex and 13 nine-cells. Two complete Hasse topological sorts traverse all 434,221 faces and 3,663,100 cover relations, so the finite acyclicity assertions are exhaustive. Forman's theorem and the absence of intermediate cells prove an integral wedge of thirteen nine-spheres. The perfect matching/bipartition certify vertex-cover number equal to ten. Independent orbit-cycle and signed-chain Lefschetz computations agree for ten rotations, giving the stated rational representation. The supplied script and output were run from the actual package directory.

value.rationale: The Desargues graph is a canonical highly symmetric cubic bipartite graph and a natural nonchordal test of dominance-complex topology. Its nonpure 13-dimensional simplicial complex has a nonobvious complete integral homotopy classification in dimension nine. The result supplies a sharpness case of Matsushita's general bound and a nontrivial order-ten rational symmetry decomposition with one fixed line. This is substantive structural information, not an arbitrary slice or a textbook consequence of the vertex-cover number. It does not claim an all-family theorem or integral equivariant splitting.
